edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Hom. in Cant. II, 5

source_text: Trabes domorum nostrarum cedri. Haec multitudinis verba sunt. Videntur autem mihi viri hoc dicere qui cum sponso sunt, de quibus superius sermo praefatus est. Domus nostra, id est ecclesia, trabibus cedrinis fulcitur, quia cedrus imputribilis est, et doctrina apostolorum et prophetarum imputribiliter ecclesiam continet.
pass_a_gloss: Beams of-our houses cedars. These of-the-multitude words are. They-seem however to-me men this to-say who with bridegroom are, about whom above speech was-prefaced. Our house, that is church, with cedar beams is-supported because cedar is incorruptible, and teaching of-apostles and prophets incorruptibly the church holds.
pass_b_english: [[The beams of our houses are cedar >> Bible:Song of Songs 1:17]]. These are words of the many. They seem to me to be spoken by the men who are with the Bridegroom, of whom speech was made above. Our house — that is, the church — is upheld by cedar beams, because cedar is incorruptible, and the teaching of apostles and prophets holds the church without decay.
notes: Song Homilia II OET; Lawson not used for wording.
